checks_run: Inspected all 60 candidate files for correctness, learner/reference separation, provenance, licensing, validation honesty, and learner usefulness.
Recorded the configured CPython and OpenJDK paths and versions; compiled all candidate Python sources with bytecode redirected outside CANDIDATE.
Ran the public suite against the sealed reference, the sealed evaluator suite, and the public suite against the untouched starter under bounded timeouts.
Ran the learner-view source check, performed an actual export, and independently audited its exact paths, entry types, modes, bytes, and forbidden roots.
Checked manifest/provenance identity fields and hashes, generated-material terms, regular-entry structure, standard-library imports, risky extraction/process patterns, and obvious secret patterns.

Ran reviewer-authored probes for compressed layers, whiteout preflight preservation, log-byte boundaries, invalid UTF-8, process-group timeout cleanup, cross-process state claims, cross-process image publication races, cleanup, and CLI domain errors.
Compared the candidate content inventory before and after validation to confirm it was not modified.
evidence: Public/reference suite: 11 tests ran and passed; sealed suite: 37 tests ran and passed.
Untouched starter: 11 tests ran and failed with 17 expected TODO NotImplementedError errors, showing that the learner scaffold was not replaced by the reference.
Student-view check reported 28 files; the actual export contained exactly the 28 sorted allowlisted regular files, all mode 0644 and byte-identical, with no evaluator roots.

Reviewer probes observed one winner from two process-level start claims, one winner from two different-content imports for one tag, and two successes sharing one object for concurrent same-content imports; no build/staging leftovers remained.

Reviewer probes passed compressed tar application, invalid derived-whiteout rejection without mutation, all specified truncation-marker ranges, UTF-8 byte budgeting, descendant process-group termination, and single-line CLI domain-error handling.

MANIFEST.yaml and PROVENANCE.json identity fields agree; their byte hashes are 4eb8b23f9c116db38a01876763e2e4f97e22c4219c9446bf949bb7e374c43123 and 266aadf01d684512a09ebed6ddd12fdbb424c6b2c27bb676147ce4df18d37705 respectively.
The candidate inventory digest was f65a641e38836de14a21804480007011b920123b7137c8fe36055f82df17c06b both before and after checks.
Claims remain limited to GENERATED and PARTIAL; productionized is false and independent validation remains required.
limitations: No upstream/network access was used, so authorship similarity, the catalog snapshot, linked-resource licensing, and factory-owned baseline/remediation identifiers were not externally corroborated.
No fuzz campaign, benchmark, profiler, transfer test, deployment, hostile multi-tenant exercise, or kernel namespace/cgroup/seccomp isolation test was performed.
The runtime is intentionally not a security boundary; subprocess log disk use, hard-crash reconciliation, filesystem/SQLite atomicity, and same-user integrity races remain documented limitations.
Checks used one POSIX environment with CPython 3.11.5. OpenJDK 21.0.5+11 was available but irrelevant to this Python-only pack.
This PASS is advisory and does not publish REVIEWED or any other validation label.
